You are working in the git repository checked out at /dateutil (a copy of the python-dateutil library). There is a bug in /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py. The symptom: the test named `dateutil.test.test_rrule.RRuleTest::testCountZero` should pass, but currently does not. Note: the exact version of that test which exercises the bug is NOT present in the repository, so you must infer the expected behaviour from the repository's own docs/docstrings and from what a test with that name would naturally check: constructing an rrule with `count=0` (e.g. `rrule(DAILY, count=0, dtstart=datetime(2003,1,1))`) and iterating it should yield ZERO occurrences (an empty list), rather than one occurrence or an error. Check `list(rrule(...))`, `len(list(rrule(...)))`, `rrule(...)[0]`, `list(rrule(...).xafter(...))`, and also `rruleset` containing such a rule.

Your job:
1. Read /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py carefully, especially the `rrule.__init__`, the `_iter` method / `_iterinfo`, `count` handling, and the `__getitem__`/`xafter` methods.
2. Find the real bug: likely the `count` is only decremented/checked in a way that allows one extra occurrence when count == 0 (e.g. `if self._count is not None and self._len >= self._count` checked after yielding, or the check `if self._count and ...` treats 0 as falsy). Investigate empirically with python, e.g. `python -c "from dateutil.rrule import *; from datetime import datetime; print(list(rrule(DAILY, count=0, dtstart=datetime(2003,1,1))))"` and with count=1, count=2 to make sure those still work.
3. Fix the bug in /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py with a minimal, targeted change (make sure `count=0` yields no occurrences while `count=None` means infinite and `count=N` yields exactly N).
4. Verify: run the full existing rrule test suite `python -m pytest dateutil/test/test_rrule.py -q` (or `python -m unittest dateutil.test.test_rrule -v` if pytest is missing) and confirm no pre-existing test regresses. Also run the whole test suite `python -m pytest dateutil/test -q` if time permits, and report any failures that also fail before your change (check with `git stash` if needed).

URGENT, work fast (a few minutes max). Repo: /dateutil (python-dateutil). File: /dateutil/dateutil/relativedelta.py. Bug: the test `dateutil.test.test_relativedelta.RelativeDeltaTest::testAbsoluteAddition` must pass (that test is not in the repo; infer from the class docstring: absolute args year/month/day/hour/minute/second/microsecond REPLACE values, plural args add). The likely bug: in `relativedelta.__add__` (the `isinstance(other, relativedelta)` branch, around lines 303-322) the absolute fields are merged with `or`, e.g. `year=other.year or self.year`, `hour=other.hour or self.hour`, `microsecond=(other.microsecond or self.microsecond)` - so an absolute value of 0 (e.g. `relativedelta(hour=0)`, `relativedelta(minute=0)`, `relativedelta(second=0)`, `relativedelta(microsecond=0)`, `relativedelta(day=0)`) is silently dropped. Fix by replacing each `other.X or self.X` with an explicit None test, e.g. `year=(other.year if other.year is not None else self.year)`, for year, month, day, weekday, hour, minute, second, microsecond (keep `leapdays=other.leapdays or self.leapdays` as is). Verify with python that `relativedelta() + relativedelta(hour=0) == relativedelta(hour=0)`, same for minute/second/microsecond/day, and that `relativedelta(year=2004) + relativedelta(month=2) == relativedelta(year=2004, month=2)`. Then run `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test/test_relativedelta.py -q` and `python -m pytest dateutil/test -q` and confirm no failures. Do NOT modify tests. Another agent may be editing the same file for a different bug (float addition): read the file right before editing, make the smallest edit, re-read after, and never revert others' changes. Report the diff and test results.

URGENT, work fast (a few minutes max). Repo: /dateutil (python-dateutil). File: /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py. Bug: the test `dateutil.test.test_rrule.RRuleTest::testStrAppendRRULEToken` must pass (not in the repo; the name means the `rrule.__str__` output must append the `RRULE:` token correctly). Read `rrule.__str__` (around lines 672-732). Currently it builds `parts = ['FREQ=' + FREQNAMES[self._freq]]` and returns `'\n'.join(output)` where output may start with `DTSTART:...`; there is no `RRULE:` token anywhere. The fix: the rule line must be prefixed with `RRULE:`, i.e. append `'RRULE:' + ';'.join(parts)` to output (so `str(rrule(DAILY, count=3, dtstart=datetime(2003,1,1)))` == 'DTSTART:20030101T000000\nRRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3'). Check the module docstring and docs/examples.rst for the expected format. Also make sure `rrulestr(str(rule))` still round-trips (the existing tests `_rrulestr_reverse_test` must keep passing) and that `rrulestr` accepts the 'RRULE:' prefix. Verify: `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test/test_rrule.py -q` and `python -m pytest dateutil/test -q` (no failures allowed). Do NOT modify tests. Another agent may be editing the same file for a different bug (count=0 in `_iter`): read the file right before editing, make the smallest edit, re-read after, never revert others' changes. Report the diff and test results.

Fix the broken case minimally. Verify with `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test/test_relativedelta.py -q` and `python -m pytest dateutil/test -q` (no failures allowed).
